listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Monday, November 2. Here is what matters today. Our lead story is a deadly plane crash in South Florida. Nine people are dead after a business jet crashed into a neighborhood. U.S. Transportation Secretary Duffy says all nine people aboard died. NPR reports the jet nosedived and erupted into a fireball near a busy roadway. The aircraft had left Austin, Texas, and was headed to the Bahamas. No cause has been given in the summary. Now the front page. In the Gulf, Qatar has led intense mediation for the past 72 hours. The aim is to stave off possible new U.S. attacks on Iran after Tuesday's midterm elections. The uncertainty has the whole region on edge. In Michigan, Representative Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers in the Senate race. She had been due to attend a unity event with Abdul El-Sayed, who beat her in the Democratic primary. And the FBI says North Korean hackers are behind the theft of six point three billion dollars from the Binance crypto exchange. In tech, Anthropic has deprecated fast mode for Claude Opus 4.8. It will be removed on November 30. Users should move to Claude Opus 5.5. Also worth a look is a popular new repo with a Claude skill that turns AI-looking interfaces into designed ones. In politics, NPR says some key races look very close on the last day before Election Day. Drop Site News reports that two people working on the Rogers campaign are also registered agents for the government of Israel. In world news, the several-day ceasefire in a Russian-occupied Ukrainian city has ended. Hundreds of residents were able to evacuate. Separately, the UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara ended after 35 years. In sports, the Rockets, now six and one, host the Celtics and look for a fourth straight home win. Braves first baseman Matt Olson won his fourth Gold Glove. And Jauan Jennings reportedly wanted to stay with the Vikings after the 49ers tried to trade for him. In Atlanta, the Beltline has revealed five options for connecting its trail and transit to MARTA rail. Georgia also set a midterm record with 2.8 million early ballots. In architecture, a house in Shimane Prefecture explores how a building can respond to the landscape through bodily experience. Another is a lakeside home designed for a single owner. In science, the Vera Rubin Observatory is shedding new light on the region beyond Neptune. And computer models suggest a striking cloud on Mars may form through surprising physics. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: 9 dead as jet nosedives and erupts into fireball near busy roadway in South Florida
lead.note: Nine people are dead after a business jet crashed into a neighborhood in South Florida. U.S. Transportation Secretary Duffy said all nine people aboard the aircraft died. NPR reports that the jet nosedived and erupted into a fireball near a busy roadway. The aircraft had departed from Austin, Texas, and was headed to the Bahamas. The summary does not give a cause for the crash. For now, the facts are limited to the deaths, the location and the flight path. Further detail on who was aboard and what went wrong will likely come in the days ahead. It is the largest loss of life in today's news, arriving on the last morning before Tuesday's midterm elections.
